turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Hi there, how are you feeling now after the surgery?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I'm okay, I guess. Still a bit groggy, but I can talk.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good. Can you tell me your pain level out of 10? Any discomfort from the incisions or inside your abdomen?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: It's about a 4, maybe 5. There's some tightness and soreness, but not too bad.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Alright, we can manage that with pain relief. Are you feeling nauseous or did you feel sick at all during or after the surgery?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, no nausea. Just a bit thirsty, but I know I can't drink yet, right?

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: That's correct for now. How's your breathing? Any tightness or difficulty breathing?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Breathing is fine. I'm a bit more conscious of my tummy, but I can breathe okay.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good. Since you had general anesthesia with a spinal, do you remember anything from the operating room?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Not really. I remember going to sleep, then waking up here. Nothing in between.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: That's expected. You have a BMI of 28.5 and are diabetic — are you feeling any signs of low sugar, like shakiness or dizziness?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, I don't feel shaky. I'm just tired, but that's probably normal after surgery.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good to hear. We'll keep an eye on your blood sugar and get you moving soon. Any other concerns?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, I think that's all. Thanks for checking on me.
